ShaderNodePreset.Name: Beauty FS
ShaderNodePreset.Description:
Beauty FS - frequency separation beauty work.
Splits the front into three bands - base tone, mid frequency blemishes and fine skin texture - then lets you soften or boost each one independently. A procedural skin texture generator can add pore level detail back in, either alongside the natural texture or in place of it once the fine band has been softened away.
Inputs: Front the image to work on Matte drives the strength of the effect ST map optional, tracks the procedural texture onto moving skin
Set the fine detail to 0 and the texture amount to around 0.5 for a full texture replacement. Leave the texture amount at 0 and pull the detail gains down for a straight softening.

Uniform.Name: front
Uniform.Tooltip: The image to retouch

Uniform.Name: stmap
Uniform.Tooltip: Optional UV pass, red and green are used as texture coordinates so the procedural texture sticks to the skin as it moves

Uniform.Name: texScale
Uniform.Tooltip: Spacing of the pore cells, in pixels of the current resolution

Uniform.Name: texAspect
Uniform.Tooltip: Stretches the texture, useful for anamorphic material or for stretching pores along a cheekbone

Uniform.Name: texRotate
Uniform.Tooltip: Rotates the texture, in degrees

Uniform.Name: texSpace
Uniform.Tooltip: Screen locks the texture to the frame. ST map reads texture coordinates from the ST map input so the texture tracks with the skin

Uniform.Name: stFlipV
Uniform.Tooltip: Flip the green channel of the ST map, for UV passes rendered with the origin at the top

Uniform.Name: texOffset
Uniform.Tooltip: Slides the texture, in pixels

Uniform.Name: texSeed
Uniform.Tooltip: Changes the random pattern without changing its character

Uniform.Name: poreAmount
Uniform.Tooltip: Weight of the cellular pore layer

Uniform.Name: poreSize
Uniform.Tooltip: How much of each cell the pore fills - small values give tight dots, large values give a soft dimpled surface

Uniform.Name: poreIrregular
Uniform.Tooltip: 0 puts the pores on a regular grid, 1 scatters them fully

Uniform.Name: poreDepthVar
Uniform.Tooltip: Randomises the depth of each pore so they are not all identical

Uniform.Name: fineAmount
Uniform.Tooltip: Weight of the fractal noise layer that sits between the pores

Uniform.Name: fineFreq
Uniform.Tooltip: Frequency of the fractal noise, relative to the pore spacing

Uniform.Name: fineOctaves
Uniform.Tooltip: Number of noise octaves - more octaves give finer structure at more cost

Uniform.Name: fineRough
Uniform.Tooltip: How much each octave contributes relative to the one before it

Uniform.Name: microAmount
Uniform.Tooltip: Weight of the finest noise layer, roughly the scale of peach fuzz

Uniform.Name: microFreq
Uniform.Tooltip: Frequency of the finest noise layer, relative to the pore spacing

Uniform.Name: warpAmount
Uniform.Tooltip: Distorts the texture coordinates so the cell structure never reads as a grid

Uniform.Name: warpFreq
Uniform.Tooltip: Frequency of the warp - low values bend large areas, high values roughen individual cells

Uniform.Name: texContrast
Uniform.Tooltip: Shapes the generated signal about zero - above 1 keeps the peaks and suppresses the flat areas

Uniform.Name: midRadius
Uniform.Tooltip: Splits fine texture from mid frequency blemishes. Roughly the size of the pores and grain you want to treat as texture, in pixels

Uniform.Name: edgeProtect
Uniform.Tooltip: Stops the blurs dragging eyebrows, lips and background across the skin. 0 is a plain gaussian, high values keep more edges but can harden the result

Uniform.Name: quality
Uniform.Tooltip: Sample stride for the blurs - drop it down while you work, put it back to Best to render

Uniform.Name: baseRadius
Uniform.Tooltip: Splits mid frequency blemishes from the underlying skin tone. Roughly the size of the blotches and shading unevenness you want to treat, in pixels

Uniform.Name: matte
Uniform.Tooltip: Drives the strength of the effect - white is full effect, black is untouched front

Uniform.Name: midDetail
Uniform.Tooltip: Gain on the mid frequency band. 1 leaves it alone, 0 removes blemishes and blotches completely, above 1 exaggerates them

Uniform.Name: fineDetail
Uniform.Tooltip: Gain on the fine band. 1 leaves the natural skin texture alone, 0 removes it ready for the procedural texture to replace it, above 1 sharpens

Uniform.Name: strength
Uniform.Tooltip: Master mix back over the front, on top of whatever the matte input is doing

Uniform.Name: texAmount
Uniform.Tooltip: Strength of the procedural skin texture. Start around 0.5 with the fine detail pulled to 0

Uniform.Name: texMode
Uniform.Tooltip: Multiply scales the texture with local brightness, which is the more photographic behaviour. Add lays it on at a constant level

Uniform.Name: texTint
Uniform.Tooltip: Per channel weighting of the texture - warm values put more structure in the red record, the way real skin does

Uniform.Name: texShading
Uniform.Tooltip: In Add mode, fades the texture out of the shadows in step with the base. Multiply mode does this on its own

Uniform.Name: matteChannel
Uniform.Tooltip: Which channel of the matte input drives the strength

Uniform.Name: invertMatte
Uniform.Tooltip: Invert the strength matte

Uniform.Name: matteGain
Uniform.Tooltip: Multiplies the matte before it is clamped, for pushing a soft matte up to solid

Uniform.Name: shadowLevel
Uniform.Tooltip: Fades the effect out below this luminance in the base. 0 is off

Uniform.Name: highlightLevel
Uniform.Tooltip: Fades the effect out above this luminance in the base, which keeps speculars intact. 100 is off

Uniform.Name: clampNegative
Uniform.Tooltip: Clamp the result at zero, so boosted detail cannot push dark pixels negative

Uniform.Name: viewMode
Uniform.Tooltip: Look at the individual bands while you set the radii. The band views are offset by 0.5 so you can see the negative half. The procedural texture view shows at least full strength, so the pattern stays visible while you dial the amount in
